name: java-springboot
description: Best practices for Spring Boot applications.

- Build: Maven (`pom.xml`) or Gradle (`build.gradle`); use Spring Boot starters such as `spring-boot-starter-web` and `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa`.
- Organize by feature/domain (e.g., `com.example.app.order`), not layer (e.g., `com.example.app.controller`).
- Always use constructor-based injection for required dependencies; declare dependency fields `private final`.
- Use `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, and `<REDACTED_USER>`/`<REDACTED_USER>` annotations appropriately to define beans.
- Configure via `application.yml` (or `application.properties`); use `<REDACTED_USER>` for type-safe properties and Spring Profiles (e.g., `application-dev.yml`, `application-prod.yml`) for environments.
- Do not hardcode secrets. Use environment variables or HashiCorp Vault/AWS Secrets Manager.
- Design consistent RESTful APIs. Use DTOs; Do not expose JPA entities directly to the client. Validate DTO payloads with Java Bean Validation (JSR 380) annotations (`<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`, `<REDACTED_USER>`).
- Provide consistent errors with a global exception handler using `<REDACTED_USER>` and `<REDACTED_USER>`. Encapsulate business logic in `<REDACTED_USER>` classes; services should be stateless.
- Use `<REDACTED_USER>` on service methods for declarative transactions, at the most granular level necessary.
- Use Spring Data JPA repositories extending `JpaRepository` or `CrudRepository`; complex queries: `<REDACTED_USER>` or JPA Criteria API. Use DTO projections to fetch only necessary data.
- Log with SLF4J. Logger: `private static final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(MyClass.class);` Use parameterized messages (e.g., `logger.info("Processing user {}...", userId);`), not concatenation.
